correctness.rationale: The degree-two vertex component of d on a positive pure-edge monomial is nonzero and target-disjoint across distinct pure-edge monomials; d of a vertex-containing monomial contributes at least three vertex factors. Every positive cocycle lies in the n-generated exterior vertex ideal whose (n+1)th power is zero. Endpoint assignment gives n closed factors with product the top monomial, which no differential can hit because it contains all m edge generators. These steps prove the real/rational claim for every simple graph. An exact-sign checker independently passes all 1,099 labelled graphs on up to five vertices. Rational cup-length equals real cup-length by extension of scalars and expansion in rational cohomology bases, even for nonstandard lattices; explicit invariant forms are only claimed real.

value.rationale: For all finite simple graphs this is a complete exact ordinary cup-length theorem, a natural ring invariant, with explicit n-fold top-class factorization. It shows strong edge-insensitivity even as manifold dimension and Betti numbers vary dramatically and supplies an explicit general LS-category lower bound. The result is not a renamed Betti count or a small parameter census; the invariance and construction concern all simple graphs.
